interest: Lawyer Tatsuji Fuse tells E. Herbert Norman how the 1910–11 High Treason case was fabricated.
overview: This file contains two diplomatic despatches from the Office of the United States Political Adviser in Tokyo to the Secretary of State in Washington between December 1945 and December 1947, classified under decimal file 894.04 (Judicial Branch of Government). The primary component (pages 1–4) is Despatch No. 127 dated December 27, 1945, from George Atcheson, Jr., transmitting an extensive confidential memorandum prepared by Canadian diplomat and historian E. Herbert Norman based on reminiscences from prominent Japanese lawyer Tatsuji Fuse regarding the 1910–1911 High Treason incident (Kotoku Shusui trial) and structural flaws in Japan's legal apparatus, particularly the traditional dominance of prosecutors over judges. The second document (page 5) is Despatch No. 1457 dated December 15, 1947, from Acting Political Adviser W. J. Sebald, reporting administrative appointments within the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, specifically naming Kumao Nishimura as Director of the Treaty Bureau and Shigeru Yosano as Chief of the Information Service.

subfiles.about: Covering despatch transmitting E. Herbert Norman's memorandum containing lawyer Tatsuji Fuse's reminiscences of the 1910–1911 Kotoku Shusui high treason trial and observations on the Japanese legal system.
subfiles.summary: George Atcheson, Jr. transmits E. Herbert Norman's memo on Tatsuji Fuse's account of the Kotoku Shusui treason trial, noting prosecutors' dominance over judges.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 127 from George Atcheson, Jr., transmitting memorandum on Kotoku Shusui treason trial and Japanese legal system

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording attorney Tatsuji Fuse's detailed reminiscences of the 1910–1911 Kotoku Shusui high treason trial, police suppression of leftist movements, and the systemic dominance of prosecutors in Japan.
subfiles.summary: E. Herbert Norman records Tatsuji Fuse's account of the fabricated 1910–11 High Treason case against Kotoku Shusui and his critique of prosecutorial power.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by E. Herbert Norman: Some Reminiscences of the High Treason Trial of 1910 and 1911: Case of KOTOKU Shusui (Denjiro) and Others

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch reporting personnel changes in the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, specifically within the Treaty Bureau and the Information Service.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports Kumao Nishimura named Treaty Bureau Director and Shigeru Yosano Chief of the Information Service.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1457 from W. J. Sebald on Recent Appointments in Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.
